paint.packing: World::Grid bitfield (CPP_WH:141): layout:7 | paint:9 | customDraw:1 | extraData:6 | paintID:9, little-endian uint32 per cell
paint.painted_test: a cell draws its PAINT (not its layout block) iff paintID != 0 (CPP_WC:861 World::GetDisplayTile, CPP_WC:947 DrawWorld)
paint.style_formula: style = paint // 47, blob = paint % 47 (CPP_BT:26-37 builds mTile_Paint style-major over 10 styles x 47 cr31 blob tiles)
paint.CORRECTION: the plan v1 said (p-1)//47. That is OFF BY ONE: the measured ranges below are exactly [47*s, 47*s+46], so the divisor has no -1.
paint.paintable_layouts_prov: CPP_WE:1421-1425 WorldEditor::PlotPaint1 paints only where mLayout==1 || mLayout==67 (the 47-blob branch); mLayout==2 has its own smaller layout and is left unpainted by our writer
paint.blob_match_rule: CPP_WE:1341-1450 GetTileMatch47 + CPP_WE:IsTileMatch -- a neighbour COUNTS AS THE SAME MATERIAL iff its paintID equals this region's paintID (NOT its layout); out of bounds counts as different
paint.blob_base_formula: base = style_paint_ranges[style][0] (CPP_WE:1323-1339 GetPaintBase returns 47*tool for tools 0..8)
paint.default_style_evidence: FLASHLEVEL.kitty: 2752 of 8238 painted cells are bucket 7, the largest share (see censuses.kitty_paint_styles)

suggested_style_per_gif_bulk._note: aesthetic suggestions only -- UNVERIFIED. The RULED default for every bulk id is 'panels'; a converter must not use these without a user flag.

kitty_file.container: int32 fileVersion, then a chunk tree; chunk = int32 payloadLen, payload, int32 childCount, children (SaveGame.cpp)
kitty_file.primitives: int32 LE; float32 LE; bool = 1 byte; String = int32 len(INCLUDING the NUL) + bytes; Point = 2 floats (rapt_iobuffer.cpp:852,881; SaveGame.cpp:286-319)
kitty_file.current_SAVEGAME_VERSION: 0x0010 (globals.h:27) -- the 11 campaign files are the OLD v1 layout written by WorldEditor's v1 path (CPP_WE:1055-1067)

grid_chunk.level_map_type: MAPTYPE = char (CPP_WH:42); the revealed-map state, left over from editor testing -- not authored content
grid_chunk.radio_subchunk: NEVER present at v1: the grid chunk has 0 children in all 11 campaign levels (World::Sync writes one at the current SAVEGAME_VERSION)
grid_chunk.summary: 5 of 11 campaign levels carry mLevelMap; 6 do not

children: 1: grid {int w, int h, uint32 cells[w*h], [MAPTYPE mLevelMap[w*h]]}
5: editor tool chunk {int mPaintID, [bool mTestedOK], [int difficulty]}
kitty_file.spawn_from_pixel: world = (col*tile_size_px, row*tile_size_px) -- NO half-tile offset. Measured in the program that READS the gif: RWIA_BIN LoadLevel @0x261dc8 (robot, id 255) and @0x261b20 (kitty, id 254) both do imul col,[tileW] / imul row,[tileH] and store the products straight into the entity Point.  The C++ side then normalises: World::LoadLevel (CPP_WC:481) calls Robot::FixPosition, which lifts the collide box out of solid and drops it to the floor (CPP_PC:322-341), so Y moves at load while X does not.  (Note World::GridToWorld, CPP_WC:200, is CENTRE-based -- cell*40+20 -- which is why campaign spawns look half-tile shifted.)

settings_donor.why: it is the flagship acceptance pair's own level, and it carries the SHORTER form of BOTH optional parts: the 71-byte extra chunk (no trailing mDied byte) and the cells-only grid chunk (no mLevelMap array).  The two go together -- see kitty_file.grid_chunk: the 5 levels with mLevelMap are exactly the 5 with the 72-byte extra chunk.  The VALUES are not load-bearing either way: all 11 campaign levels carry byte-identical values for every field of this chunk.

fields.name: mDied
fields.note: PRESENT only in the 72-byte variant (6 of 11 levels); omit it to reproduce 71 B

editor_tool_chunk.note: mPaintID is the editor's next paint-REGION id. A writer that paints n regions must leave this above the highest paintID it wrote.

settings_donor.runtime_only_fields: customDraw and extraData are 0 in ALL 11 campaign levels -- they are computed at load (CPP_WC:2790-2806), so a writer must emit 0.
